clue.text: For instance, a rain-cloud occurs when the tide is in

definitions.meaning: a rain-cloud is, whimsically, a body of moisture held up in the sky
the moment the sea reaches its fullest point on the shore

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a playful literal reading: a rain-cloud is water that sits high above us. The second is the everyday term for the top of the tide.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both the peak of the tide and, read literally, moisture held aloft in a cloud.

clue.text: Wrongly enlarge a fighting man

indicators.note: letters set down wrongly are out of their proper order, so they must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone mistakenly blows up a photograph of a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrongly' tells you to rearrange the seven letters of ENLARGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A general is a senior army officer, so a fighting man in the broad sense.

clue.text: Put down the script!

parts.note: read as an instruction to set words on paper rather than to discard a play's text

explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a director telling an actor to drop the script; cryptically it asks you to commit words to paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To put words down on paper in script is to compose them by hand.

clue.text: Look after no back part of the body

parts.note: to tend is to look after

indicators.note: in a down clue, back says the word no is read in the reverse direction

explanation.surface: A carer is told to tend someone without minding their back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look after' is the verb TEND; 'back' reverses the little word 'no'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendon is a cord of tissue joining muscle to bone, a part of the body.

clue.text: Pace it? I'd pray to change it!

indicators.note: the letters are asked to change their arrangement into something new

explanation.surface: Someone hopes prayer will alter the speed of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges IT plus IDPRAY (from 'I'd pray'), eight letters in all; the final 'it' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapidity is speed or quickness, which is what pace means here.

clue.text: In a place of confinement, our fine quality shows itself

indicators.note: In says the word our sits inside the place of confinement

parts.note: a cage is a place where a creature is confined

explanation.surface: Locked up, we still show our finest character.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests prisoners showing spirit; 'In' tucks the clue's 'our' inside a cage.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage, or bravery, is a fine quality of character.

clue.text: Wild West's dishes

indicators.note: wild letters are unruly and out of order, so they must be rearranged

parts.note: the letters of West's, the S included

explanation.surface: Food from the Wild West, cowboy cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges WESTS, the letters of 'West's' with its S counted.
explanation.definitionFit: Stews are slow-cooked dishes of meat and vegetables.

clue.text: One cut out to be an artist — how appropriate!

definitions.text: One cut out to be an artist — how appropriate!

parts.words: One cut out to be an artist — how appropriate!
parts.note: the idiom cut out to be, meaning suited for, is apt for an artist who cuts and carves his work

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut out to be' normally just means naturally suited; here it also describes literally the cutting work this artist does in stone or wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A carver of stone or wood is an artist whose work is done by cutting.

clue.text: Notice it's over a barred place

definitions.text: Notice it's over a barred place

parts.words: Notice it's over a barred place
parts.note: a notice hung above a place with a bar, that is a pub, rather than a prison

explanation.walkthrough: 'Barred place' suggests a jail; it means a place with a bar, a pub, whose board hangs above the door.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub's painted board is a notice displayed over a drinking place.

clue.text: May be hung or drawn — but not quartered!

definitions.text: May be hung or drawn — but not quartered!

parts.words: May be hung or drawn — but not quartered!
parts.note: plays on the old punishment hanged, drawn and quartered: artwork is hung on walls and drawn by artists

explanation.walkthrough: The clue echoes the old English punishment of being hanged, drawn and quartered; a painting or sketch is hung and drawn, but nobody cuts it in four.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting or sketch is something drawn and then hung on a wall.

clue.text: Costs nothing to possess such property it seems

parts.note: something that costs nothing is free
to hold is to possess

explanation.surface: A property owner seems to keep land without paying for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it seems' is a link: the pieces read literally as owning something free.
explanation.definitionFit: Freehold is outright ownership of land or buildings, a form of property tenure.

clue.text: Burdens the boys with love

indicators.note: with here means having inside, so love is held within the boys

parts.note: lads are boys
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Boys in love find it a heavy load to bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' puts O (love, zero in tennis) inside LADS.
explanation.definitionFit: Loads are heavy weights carried, which is what burdens are.

clue.text: Last World Council overthrown, produces a leader

indicators.note: something overthrown is upset and thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, is a world council

explanation.surface: The final world body is toppled, and a ruler emerges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overthrown' rearranges LAST plus UN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultan is the ruler of a Muslim state, so a leader.

clue.text: Advances to ring round one who came before us

indicators.note: ring round tells us these clue words go round the answer, enclosing it within their letters

explanation.surface: Someone moves forward to encircle a forebear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' says the answer is enclosed by 'Advances to ring': it runs from the end of 'Advances' into the first letter of 'ring'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancestor is a forebear, someone from whom we are descended.

clue.text: Speaks repetitively, though not making the meaning properly clear!

definitions.text: Speaks repetitively, though not making the meaning properly clear!

parts.words: Speaks repetitively, though not making the meaning properly clear!
parts.note: describes halting speech in which sounds are repeated, garbling what is said

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a description of a speech impediment, with the hint that the speaker struggles to get words out cleanly.
explanation.definitionFit: A speaker who repeats initial sounds involuntarily is hesitating and faltering in speech.

clue.text: Add lustre, we hear, to the resort

indicators.note: we hear says the word for adding lustre is said aloud, giving a place name

parts.note: to brighten is to add lustre

explanation.surface: Someone talks of polishing up a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIGHTON is a seaside resort on the south coast of England; it is pronounced much like BRIGHTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Brighton is a famous English seaside resort in Sussex.

clue.text: An open letter, might one say?

definitions.text: An open letter, might one say?

parts.words: An open letter, might one say?
parts.note: an open letter is usually a public protest, but here a message anyone can read because it has no envelope

explanation.walkthrough: 'Open letter' suggests a published protest; here it is a message written on a card with no envelope, open to the postman's eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A card sent through the mail without an envelope is a message anyone can read.

clue.text: Tears up its intoxicants

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word for tears is read from bottom to top

parts.note: rips are tears

explanation.surface: Someone tears up a bottle's label in drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RIPS into SPIR, followed by ITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirits are strong distilled drinks such as whisky and gin, intoxicants.

clue.text: Vulgar jokes, if broad enough, may bring the house down!

definitions.text: Vulgar jokes, if broad enough, may bring the house down!

parts.words: Vulgar jokes, if broad enough, may bring the house down!
parts.note: quips that get a huge laugh, and also splits in a wall that, if wide, can make a building collapse

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring the house down' means win roaring applause, but also literally make a building fall; the word means both jokes and fissures.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both quick jokes and fissures in a structure.

clue.text: Touch part of an electrical device

definitions.meaning: a conducting piece through which current passes

explanation.definitionFit: The word means touching, and also the conductor in a switch or plug where circuits meet.

clue.text: Coward put him on a par with Imperial Englishmen!

definitions.text: Coward put him on a par with Imperial Englishmen!

parts.words: Coward put him on a par with Imperial Englishmen!
parts.note: Noel Coward's 1931 song pairs crazed canines with Englishmen of the Empire who go out in the midday sun

explanation.walkthrough: Coward is not a timid person but Noel Coward, the English playwright and songwriter, whose famous comic song lumps rabid animals together with colonial Englishmen braving the tropical noon.
explanation.definitionFit: The song title pairs a rabid canine with Englishmen, so the answer is the creature named.

clue.text: Raise new sign — it's unearthly

indicators.note: new signals that the letters are made into a fresh word

explanation.surface: Someone puts up a new notice about something otherworldly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges RAISE. The sign is a zodiac sign, a constellation in the heavens, hence 'unearthly'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ram is the first sign of the zodiac, a group of stars far beyond Earth.

clue.text: Little power unit went before French, so there's plenty sounds like the rest!

indicators.note: went before says the power unit comes first, ahead of the French piece

parts.note: amp, short for ampere, is a unit of electric current
le is the French word for the

explanation.surface: A small generator was set up before the French arrived, so there was enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' signals the shortening of ampere to AMP; LE stands for French, being the French definite article.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ample is plentiful, more than enough.

clue.text: The miser is coming to understand

definitions.meaning: a miser is greedy and avaricious, so this describes what he is
taking in or comprehending an idea

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition borrows 'is': a miser is greedy. The second is the mental sense of grasping an idea.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both avaricious and in the act of comprehending.

clue.text: A bit sounds like the rest!

indicators.note: sounds like tells us the word for rest is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: peace is rest, a quiet state

explanation.surface: A snippet that resembles the remainder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the rest' looks like 'the remainder', but it means rest as quiet, PEACE, which is pronounced like PIECE.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a portion or fragment, a bit of something.

clue.text: Let the line lengthen, like the wages clerk?

definitions.meaning: to let a rope or fishing line run out gradually
a clerk handing over wages has disbursed the money

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is releasing rope or line; the other is literally handing out money, as a wages clerk does.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both slackened a rope off gradually and disbursed money.

clue.text: Apparently very conservative way to pass on, involving great struggle

definitions.meaning: describes a stubborn traditionalist who resists all change

definitions.text: way to pass on, involving great struggle
definitions.meaning: read literally, a death fought against to the end

explanation.walkthrough: 'Apparently' is a link hinting that the second sense is a literal reading of the phrase: perishing only after a long fight.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names an intransigent traditionalist and, literally, a death resisted with great struggle.

clue.text: Left alone in the wrong way, as it were

definitions.text: Left alone in the wrong way, as it were

parts.words: Left alone in the wrong way, as it were
parts.note: uncared for, and playfully a vote gone wrong, as if chosen negatively

explanation.walkthrough: The second half splits the word playfully as a negative form of being voted in: chosen at the polls the wrong way round, as it were.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left unattended or uncared for has been ignored and overlooked.
